questions.question: When passing, when should you move back into the right lane?

options.text: When you are one vehicle length ahead of the other vehicle.
When you can see both headlights of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror.
When you are 50 feet ahead of the other vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see both headlights of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Wait until you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror before returning to the right lane. This means you have enough space between you and the other vehicle.

questions.question: When entering a freeway, how should you check traffic?

options.text: Use your rearview and side mirrors.
Use your rearview mirror.
Use your side mirror and look over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your side mirror and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Use your side mirror and look over your shoulder to see traffic on the freeway. This helps you spot vehicles and merge safely.

questions.question: Which lane should you be in to make a left turn from a one-way street?

options.text: The lane nearest the left curb.
The lane nearest the center of the street.
The lane nearest the right curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane nearest the left curb.
questions.explanation: Always turn from the lane closest to where you want to go. For a left turn on a one-way street, use the lane nearest the left curb.

questions.question: What must you do at an intersection with a flashing red light?

options.text: Stop completely, let oncoming traffic and pedestrians pass, then proceed.
Slow down and proceed with caution.
Stop completely and wait until the light turns green.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, let oncoming traffic and pedestrians pass, then proceed.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. Come to a complete stop, make sure it is safe, then proceed.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you never do?

options.text: Change lanes while inside an intersection.
Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.
Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes while inside an intersection.
questions.explanation: Never change lanes while inside an intersection. Always look over your shoulder to check your blind spot and watch for other drivers entering your lane.

questions.question: When merging onto the freeway, what speed should you drive?

options.text: At or near the speed of freeway traffic.
Five to 10 mph slower than freeway traffic.
The posted speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: At or near the speed of freeway traffic.
questions.explanation: Merge onto the freeway at or near the speed of traffic already on the freeway.

questions.question: When do large trucks lose speed?

options.text: When driving up long or steep hills.
When driving in long, gradual curves.
When driving down long, gradual hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: When driving up long or steep hills.
questions.explanation: Large trucks lose speed going uphill because they take longer to accelerate. Give trucks extra space on hills.

questions.question: When is highway pavement most slippery?

options.text: After it has been raining for several hours.
When rain first starts.
After it has been raining for one to two hours.

questions.correctAnswerText: When rain first starts.
questions.explanation: Pavement is most slippery when rain first begins. Dirt and oil on the road mix with water, creating a greasy surface.

questions.question: What is the best way to avoid dangerous driving situations?

options.text: Know what is happening around your vehicle.
Turn off the radio.
Always keep your eyes focused straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Know what is happening around your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Always watch what is happening around your vehicle—front, sides, and rear. This helps you spot problems and react safely.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow centerline mean?

options.text: Passing is not allowed.
You can pass on the right when the way ahead is clear.
You can pass on the left when the way ahead is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass on the left when the way ahead is clear.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line on your side means you can cross it to pass when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: You should signal to turn ____ before you start a turn.

options.text: 100 feet
50 feet
10 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 100 feet
questions.explanation: You must signal at least 100 feet before you turn or change lanes. This tells other drivers what you plan to do. Keep signaling until you finish the turn or lane change.

questions.question: You arrive at a four-way stop at the same time as the driver on your left. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The driver on your left has the right-of-way.
You have the right-of-way.
Whoever is signaling to make a turn has the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: When two cars arrive at a four-way stop at the same time, the car on the right has the right-of-way.

questions.question: Do not use high beam headlights in fog or mist because:

options.text: The light will reflect back into your eyes.
Approaching vehicles might not see you.
Vehicles behind you may follow too closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: The light will reflect back into your eyes.
questions.explanation: In fog or mist, high beam headlights reflect back into your eyes. Use low beams instead.

questions.question: To avoid glare from an oncoming car's headlights:

options.text: Look briefly toward the right side of the road.
Stay focused on the centerline on the road.
Flash your high beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look briefly toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Glance briefly toward the right side of the road to avoid the bright lights. Then look ahead again to see where the other car is.

questions.question: Which statement is true about driving and taking medications?

options.text: Most cold medications can make a person drowsy.
Over-the-counter medications cannot impair driving ability if taken in the recommended dosages.
Medications are safe to take at any time, if prescribed by a doctor.

questions.correctAnswerText: Most cold medications can make a person drowsy.
questions.explanation: All medications, including over-the-counter cold and allergy medicines, can make you drowsy and hurt your driving. It is your job to know how your medications affect your driving.

questions.question: If a child is about to run into the street, you should:

options.text: Start to prepare to slow down.
Flash your headlights.
Sound a sharp blast of your horn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sound a sharp blast of your horn.
questions.explanation: Use a sharp horn blast when a child or pedestrian is about to step into the street in front of your car.

questions.question: A driver license is a:

options.text: Right, not a privilege.
Privilege, not a right.
Requirement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Privilege, not a right.
questions.explanation: A driver license is a privilege. You must earn it and keep it.

questions.question: You should always travel:

options.text: At the speed of vehicles surrounding you.
At the speed limit.
At a speed appropriate for road and weather conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: At a speed appropriate for road and weather conditions.
questions.explanation: Choose your speed based on road conditions, weather, and the legal speed limit. Never drive above the speed limit. Slow down when conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: You are approaching an intersection with a steady yellow traffic light and have not entered yet. You should:

options.text: Speed up to beat the red light.
Reduce you speed and proceed carefully through the intersection.
Come to a safe stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a safe stop.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means prepare to stop. If you are already in the intersection, leave it quickly.

questions.question: To avoid hydroplaning in rain, you should:

options.text: Drive at a speed appropriate for ideal conditions.
Apply your brakes as soon as your car starts to skid.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when your tires lose contact with the road and ride on top of the water. Slow down in wet conditions to prevent this.

questions.question: If the rear of your vehicle skids to the left, what should you do?

options.text: Do not turn your steering wheel.
Turn your steering wheel to the left.
Turn your steering wheel to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel to the left.
questions.explanation: If you skid on a wet or icy road, remove your foot from the accelerator and avoid the brakes. Turn your steering wheel in the direction the rear is sliding. If you have anti-lock brakes, press them firmly and steer straight.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road to the right is one-way only.
There is a detour to the right for road construction.
The road ahead turns sharply.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead turns sharply.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs have black markings. They alert you to hazards ahead. This sign tells you to slow down for a sharp turn in the road.

questions.question: If an oncoming driver does not dim their headlights, where should you look?

options.text: At the center of the road.
At the right side of the road.
Straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: At the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: If an oncoming driver does not dim their lights, look toward the right side of the road. This keeps you from being blinded and helps you see the road to stay on course.

questions.question: At an intersection where you cannot see cross traffic, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down and look both ways.
Keep your speed and look both ways.
Stop, then move forward slowly until you can see both directions clearly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, then move forward slowly until you can see both directions clearly.
questions.explanation: Slow down when approaching an intersection. If your view is blocked, stop completely. Move forward slowly until you can see clearly in both directions.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Always stop at the crosswalk.
Stop at the crosswalk until a crossing guard signals you.
Be ready to stop if children are in the crosswalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop if children are in the crosswalk.
questions.explanation: This five-sided sign means you are near a school. Watch for children and stop if any are using the crosswalk.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Parking reserved for people with disabilities.
Slow-moving vehicle.
No U-turn allowed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Parking reserved for people with disabilities.
questions.explanation: This sign marks parking spaces for people with disability license plates, disabled veteran plates, or disability placards.

questions.question: When can you move back to your original lane after passing a vehicle?

options.text: When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
When you have cleared the front bumper of the passed vehicle.
When you are 50 feet ahead of the passed vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Return to your original lane only when you can see the other vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror. This ensures you have enough space to move safely in front.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A railroad crossing is ahead. Be ready to stop.
You will always stop at this railroad crossing.
Stop and wait for a signal before crossing the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: A railroad crossing is ahead. Be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a railroad crossing ahead. Look and listen for trains. Slow down and be prepared to stop. Wait for any trains to pass before crossing.

questions.question: On a short entrance ramp with no acceleration lane, how should you enter the interstate?

options.text: Enter the far-right lane immediately and speed up to match traffic.
Use the shoulder to speed up to match traffic.
Speed up only after you find a gap in traffic, then enter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up only after you find a gap in traffic, then enter.
questions.explanation: Speed up only after you identify a safe gap in traffic. Wait stopped on the ramp until a gap appears before entering the interstate.

questions.question: When a school bus is picking up or dropping off children, what must you do?

options.text: Stop, no matter which direction you are traveling.
Stop only if you are traveling in the same direction.
Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, no matter which direction you are traveling.
questions.explanation: When a school bus is picking up or dropping off passengers, you must stop completely before reaching the bus. This is true regardless of which direction you are traveling.
